title: Cluster connectivity runbook + interactive repair steps for Private Console
creator: Asha Kapur
description:
Goal: design an integrated runbook surface in the Private Console that guides operators through diagnosing and repairing cluster connectivity issues (inter-region peering, subnet misconfigurations, firewall rules, and routing) with a combination of contextual guidance, one-click remediation actions (where safe), and an interactive stepper that records attempted fixes. The surface should reduce mean time to repair for tenant connectivity incidents and decrease reliance on playbook PDFs or Slack handoffs.

Scope: UX flows for (1) automated incident detection screen that links to the runbook, (2) an interactive stepper with prefilled checks and suggested commands, (3) a safety modal for any mutating repair action with rollback guidance, (4) an audit trail of attempted repairs attached to the incident timeline, (5) a compact summary card for dashboard thumbnails and per-tenant status. Excludes: backend implementation of repairs (handled by ENG), long-form docs migration (handled by PM).

Design constraints: must work within Private Console’s existing compact layout and be accessible for keyboard navigation and screen readers. Repair actions must require explicit confirmation and show estimated risk and impact. When possible, present non-destructive diagnostics first.

Acceptance criteria: (1) clickable prototype (Figma) covering happy path + two failure modes (peering failure and subnet overlap), (2) annotated handoff docs for ENG describing states, API hooks, and required telemetry, (3) usability notes from at least 3 SRE/ops reviewers, (4) integration points documented for audit logs and RBAC checks.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with interactive stepper for diagnostic->repair->verify
